title: Semantics-first invocation shim: name resolution, parameter normalization, and streaming fallback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: ship a runtime shim that lets Redwood customers call OpenAI-style tools and older 'legacy function' surfaces interchangeably with predictable behavior. The shim must resolve ambiguous tool names, coerce and validate parameters into the expected schema, preserve provenance for auditing, and provide a streamed-invocation fallback path for long-lived tools. This ticket covers design, a compatibility implementation in the runtime proxy, tests, and a staged rollout plan to minimize customer regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Requests using OpenAI-style tool names (with common punctuation/aliasing) map to the canonical tool/function in >= 99.5% of production traces after thresholds tune-in
Parameter coercion converts common scalar mismatches (string->number, number->string, single->array) according to a configurable policy without dropping unknown fields

Streaming fallback: when a tool declares 'streamable' and the client requested streaming, the shim maintains a streaming connection and sends incremental tool output with invocation-provenance headers
Backwards-compat toggle: an internal feature flag allows opting into strict-name-resolution; default remains permissive until beta sign-off
End-to-end tests exist for OpenAI-style tool call, legacy function call, alias resolution, and streaming fallback; local CI and staging pass
Telemetry emitted: alias_match_rate, coercion_count, streaming_fallback_rate, invocation_latency_p50/p95 with and without shim enabled
progress_updates: 2025-02-13: Kickoff meeting with PM and runtime team. Agreed 'semantics-first' approach: prioritize preserving intent over exact name equality.
2025-02-18: Prototype alias table using fuzzy matching (trigram + edit-distance) wired into the proxy. Basic bench shows <0.5ms median added latency for nominal traffic.
2025-02-24: Implemented param normalization layer with a configurable coercion policy; initial heuristics for number/string/boolean conversion added.
2025-02-28: Design review with Security and Privacy. Decided to add invocation provenance headers and redact PII in telemetry. Security requested a KMS-backed audit blob for enterprise customers.

2025-03-03: Streaming fallback prototype: when tool advertises stanza-based output, runtime opens streaming tunnel and forwards partial chunks with sequence IDs. Basic integration tests pass in staging.
2025-03-04: MVP branch created. Preparing PR and test matrix. Feature flag 'shim_semantics_v1' added for controlled rollout.
decisions: Use a layered resolver: (1) exact canonical match, (2) alias table, (3) fuzzy-match with deterministic tie-breaker, (4) fallback to legacy function name if explicitly enabled
Coercion policy is opt-in per workspace project with defaults: permissive for dev workspaces, strict for enterprise workspaces
Streaming fallback will preserve KV-cache semantics: partial tool outputs are buffered for the model's context window but emitted incrementally to client
Telemetry exposes anonymized fingerprints rather than raw tool params to avoid leaking customer data in metrics
tradeoffs: Permissive name resolution reduces friction but risks silent model-tool mismatches; mitigated with telemetry and an opt-in strict mode
On-the-fly coercion improves user experience but may mask schema bugs in downstream tools; mitigation: emit coercion_count and provide optional validation failures
Streaming fallback adds complexity in routing and cache coherence; benefit is reduced tail latency for long-running tools and better UX for streaming-first clients
tech_notes: Alias table format: {canonical: string, aliases: [string], priority: int}. We'll persist as a sharded in-memory store with periodic hot reload from config bucket.
Fuzzy matching: combine trigram similarity + normalized levenshtein; threshold tunable per workspace. Use library X for speed and deterministic results across languages.
Parameter normalizer runs before runtime kernel selection so quantization/serialization paths can account for shape changes.
Provenance headers: X-RW-Invoke-Id, X-RW-Resolver-Path (ex: exact->alias->fuzzy), X-RW-Coercions (summary). These are recorded in audit blobs for Private deployments.

GH: redwood/console#402 - feature flag UI and event inspector rows

test_plan: Unit: resolver tie-breaker edge cases, coercion heuristics, header emission
Integration: end-to-end calls from SDK -> proxy -> tool runner with streaming enabled/disabled
Regression: run legacy function call corpus (500K historical traces) through shim in staging and assert no >0.1% semantic regression alerts
Load: synthetic spike to measure latency impact at 99th percentile with alias table enabled
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal dogfood): enable shim for internal Redwood org only for 1 week
Phase 1 (beta customers): invite 5 customers to opt-in, monitor alias_match_rate and coercion_count
Phase 2 (controlled enable): enable permissive mode by default for all dev workspaces behind feature flag; strict mode available on request
Phase 3 (gradual default flip): if metrics stable for 2 weeks and no major regressions, flip default to permissive-by-design with telemetry nudges to opt into strict validation
Rollback: feature flag off; fallback to pure name equality routing
metrics: alias_match_rate: fraction of calls resolved via alias/fuzzy paths
coercion_count: number of param coercions per 1k invocations
streaming_fallback_rate: fraction of invocations that used streaming path
invocation_success_rate: tool invocation success after resolution
latency_p50_p95: compare with and without shim enabled
